applied_items.content:
Gate lists. `chough gate list [--json]` SHALL number every open human gate of every open session in the project from 1, with the stage it holds and the native step it drives (REQ-cli-030). It SHALL give each a one-screen summary of at most 24 lines and 4,096 bytes, with:
- what changed: the files, insertions and deletions since the change's base, leaving out `.chough/`, the knowledge directory and SpecSync lifecycle bookkeeping, and naming the five files with the most changed lines among the rest (#190). At a gate that drives approval, the change's own definition, the Markdown files under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` (its `change.md`, deltas, plan and other artifacts), is what the human approves, so the summary SHALL count those files and name them first, never leaving them out as bookkeeping. The base is the change's own `base_commit` (from its `state.json`), so an earlier change on the same branch is not counted again. The base is instead the merge base of HEAD with the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `main`) in two cases: when that merge base is not an ancestor of the `base_commit`, meaning default-branch work was merged or rebased in after the change began (#190), and when the change records no `base_commit`. A merge base that is HEAD itself, as on the default branch, is not used. With no usable base, the summary says the base is unknown;
- the tests: how many cases passed, failed and were not run, by the latest observation of each case that links a requirement the change's deltas add or modify, or that the session's observations name, with the failing case IDs;
- the risks: the first 8 lines of the change's `plan.md` section "Risks", or "none recorded";
- a diff link: the GitHub compare URL from the base to HEAD when `origin` is a GitHub remote, otherwise `git diff <base>..<HEAD>`.

Each summary's digest SHALL be the SHA-256 of its text. The list SHALL be saved as `.chough/local/gate-lists/<list>.json`, where `<list>` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the list. Listing SHALL make no native read and write no tracked file. The list SHALL end with how to reply: `chough gate record` for the gates whose change is not verifying, and `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for each gate whose change is verifying.

`chough gate record <list> --gates <n>[,<n>...] --decided-by <who> --words <words> --where <where> --recorded-by <agent>` SHALL close each named gate as `chough checkpoint --close-gate` would with the four values (REQ-cli-050), and its relay SHALL carry that gate's `summary_digest` and the `list` (REQ-history-014). It SHALL close all the named gates or none. Before writing anything, it SHALL refuse:
- an unknown list, a number not on it, a listed gate that is no longer open, or a gate whose summary's digest has changed, each naming `chough gate list`;
- a gate whose change's `state.json` state is `verifying`, naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` with the relay, and giving as the reason that such a gate closes through the ship, which runs the review as the human and closes the gate after the native ship, never that Chough's records may not be written;
- more than one named gate that drives a native step, naming the gates to record one at a time.

A named gate that drives a native step SHALL run it as the decided human (REQ-records-008) before any gate is closed.

Acceptance Criteria
- `gate list` numbers each open gate with a summary naming what changed, the tests, the risks and a diff link, at most 24 lines, and the SHA-256 digest of its text; the list is saved under `.chough/local/gate-lists/` and no tracked file changes.
- One `gate record` reply naming two listed gates closes both, each relay keeping the same words and its own summary digest; a gate left off the reply stays open.
- An unknown list, a number not listed, a gate no longer open and a summary changed since listing are each refused with nothing written, and listing again then recording succeeds.
- A gate whose change is verifying is refused, naming `chough change ship` with `--list` and `--gate`, which then ships and closes it with its digest.
- Two named gates that both drive a native step are refused with nothing run or written; one such gate with gates that drive nothing runs its step once and closes all of them.
- #190: with a one-line product edit, 300 changed records under `.chough/` and `knowledge/`, and 200 files merged from main after the base, the summary counts one file and names it.
- For a second native change on one branch, the summary's what changed counts only that change's own files since its `base_commit`, not the earlier change's; with default-branch work merged in after it began, it counts from the merge base, as #190's criterion requires.
- At a scope gate, the summary's what changed counts and names the change's deltas and plan under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` first, while its `state.json` and `approvals.json` stay left out.
- With a verifying change's review gate open, `gate list` ends naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for it and offers no `gate record` for it, and the `gate record` refusal gives the ship as its reason, with no claim that Chough's records may not be written.

applied_items.content:
Focused next action. `chough next` SHALL print a compact action view, separate from the full `chough status` report: the objective; the current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers; the recorded native change with its read state, summary state, approval and correction validity, terminal evidence validity, native next action and approved-delta result; the next valid action with its reason and, when one applies, its command; the gate for the next main stage; awaiting-human gates; blockers; the checkpoint's open questions; open acceptance-blocking bug IDs with the count of other open bugs; only the referenced observations that are not current, with counts for the rest; the most recent checkpoint decisions, at most 5 with their total, showing the kind and reason of entries that follow the `decided:`, `rejected:` or `failed:` prefix convention and other entries whole; the latest failed observation by its recorded observation time, with the status of each bug that links it; and a pointer to each module's native lesson source with the count and bounded paths of archived SpecSync lesson bundles, without reading lesson text or tracking which bundles were folded; the bundles named SHALL be the newest 3 by recorded finalization timestamp, then directory, with an unreadable timestamp sorting oldest, the same 3 that `knowledge/index.md` links (REQ-cli-043). `chough status` SHALL report the same open questions, all of them, in its checkpoint section. It SHALL print text by default and the same fields as JSON with `--json`, and each form SHALL be at most 16384 bytes, with every list bounded, its total stated and any truncation marked. The same records SHALL give byte-identical output; ordering SHALL use recorded fields and names, never file modification times. At plan, while the native change waits for its definition approval, the next valid action SHALL name the human scope gate, opened with `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>" --drives approve` when none is open and closed with `chough checkpoint --close-gate` and the human's decision, and neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`, so no agent is routed to approve its own scope; an approval on authority the human gave in advance stays as REQ-cli-029 describes. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL derive the next valid action from the same rules and SHALL each make at most one native status read. The move into done archives the session (REQ-history-006), after which `chough next` refuses with "no open session" and names `chough session new <key>`. A session stays open at done only while an authorized release is still ahead or unfolded inbox entries keep it open; then, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action SHALL name, release first, `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, since the session archives itself only at the move from release into done; otherwise, while inbox entries are unfolded, including after that move, it SHALL name `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`. It SHALL do so rather than repeat the checkpoint's next action, and SHALL NOT recommend a stage reset. A stage reset SHALL replace the checkpoint's next action. In an earlier main stage, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence and no pause, human gate or blocking bug applies, the next valid action SHALL NOT continue the stage; it SHALL say the change is archived and recommend the new cycle, a stage reset that carries a reason followed by a new native change, except at accept, where it SHALL recommend recording done first, with `chough stage advance`, which archives the session. An archived change finalized no later than the latest reset, or reached directly by one, is the previous cycle's: before done the action SHALL keep the reset's guidance and, when the next gate is refused, name `specsync change new`, never the archived refusal or another reset. With no native change recorded, a refused `refused:no-native-change` gate SHALL name `specsync change new`, not a bare status read. The next valid action SHALL guide a fresh agent through every stage (#76): right after `chough init` at intent with no criteria referenced, it SHALL say to capture or read the intent and name `hi check`, then `chough context`; at test, it SHALL name `chough cases select` and `chough cases run` for the selected cases, and `chough bug add` for a referenced case whose latest run failed with no bug; at accept while the native change is verifying, it SHALL say the human reviews next and SHALL never suggest an agent review: for a decision to ship it SHALL name `chough change ship <id> --close-gate "<gate>"` with the relay of REQ-cli-050, which runs the review as the human, ships and closes the gate only after the native ship (REQ-cli-059), so nothing under `.chough/` changes between `change check --commit` and finalize; for a decision not to ship, `chough checkpoint --close-gate` with `--verdict block`; with no review gate open it SHALL first name `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<review>" --holds accept --drives review` and, while SpecSync's verification counts Chough's records (REQ-records-014), SHALL say to commit that gate and run `chough change check <id>` again before the ship; and the waiting action for an open review gate SHALL name the same ship. A gate close that leaves no open gate holding the current stage (REQ-cli-050) SHALL set the checkpoint's next action to the step that decision allows, and `chough next` SHALL never name itself as the next action: `chough stage advance` after an approval or the close of a gate that drives nothing, `chough change ship <id>` after a review pass, `chough stage back --to build` after a review block, and, after a `--no-native` close, recording the next action the decision calls for with `chough checkpoint --next-action`. At accept while the native change is approved or implementing, the next valid action SHALL name the review preparation of the workflow's accept step in order, `chough change check <id> --no-commit` first when the change's deltas add or modify requirements, then the affected cases, the review gate, the commit and `chough change check <id>`, and SHALL NOT show a refused gate or a bare native status read as the action. Local bug backlog. The helper SHALL keep each bug as one Markdown record, `.chough/bugs/<id>.md` (REQ-records-001), whose front matter gives `kind: bug`, `id`, `aliases`, `title`, `status`, `classification`, `scope`, `impact`, `criteria`, `requirements`, `cases`, `evidence` (the linked evidence IDs), `receipts` (the receipt fields of REQ-history-006 for linked evidence no longer in an open session), `regression_baseline`, `fixture`, `environment`, `revision`, `found_by` (the actor, REQ-records-007), `fixed_in`, `duplicate_of`, `related`, `created` and `updated`, where `regression_baseline`, `fixture`, `fixed_in` and `duplicate_of` are written only when set and a missing one reads as empty, and whose body gives `# <title>` and the paragraphs What happened (the symptom and actual behavior), Steps (the trigger, labelled `Trigger:`, then each step), Expected, Why it matters and Fix (`Not fixed yet.` until `chough bug update --fix <text>` sets it, each set also logged; marking a bug verified while its Fix still says `Not fixed yet.` SHALL replace that with a line naming the passing observation and its revision), then `## Log`, an append-only list with one dated entry per report, note, evidence link and status change. It SHALL list open bugs for a fresh session and SHALL search existing records by symptom, trigger and affected IDs before a new record is added. A bug SHALL remain unverified until a failed observation is linked, and a regression classification SHALL require a passed observation at an ancestor revision. A bug SHALL read as reproduced and later passed, and SHALL accept the verified status, only when a present linked passed observation was observed strictly after its most recent present linked failed observation; a receipt counts as present, and an observation shown as removed (REQ-records-009) does not. Additional evidence SHALL be appended to the Log, never overwriting anything. `chough bug add` and `chough bug update` given `--observation` with an evidence entry of the active session SHALL also add the bug to that session's checkpoint (`checkpoint --bug`, REQ-records-004), so the session's story names the bugs found in it. A bug in another tool's behaviour MAY be closed as `fixed-upstream` with `bug update --status fixed-upstream --note <text>`, the note naming the upstream fix and who checked it where; it is a closed status, as `verified`, `duplicate` and `wont-fix` are, needs no Chough observation, and SHALL never read as verified by Chough. The helper SHALL render a report candidate and SHALL NOT publish it. Every new bug SHALL be named by REQ-records-003 from its title, the same for manual `bug add` and automatic failure capture, and written by create-new; an update SHALL NOT rename the record, even when its title has changed. Every `BUG-NNNN` and `BUG-<slug>-<hex>` ID from 0.5.x SHALL resolve as an alias, and duplicate and related links SHALL resolve in either direction across aliases and new names. Documentation SHALL state that Chough 0.5.x cannot read 0.6.0 bug records. Trace: FLOW-8, LIFE-5, LIFE-8, DRIVE-25, DRIVE-27.

Acceptance Criteria
- A sample failure becomes a reproduced and classified bug; a second report of the same symptom is found by search and its evidence is appended to the Log.
- A regression classification without a passed observation at an ancestor revision is refused.
- An out-of-scope bug stays in the open backlog without changing the checkpoint scope.
- Rendering a report candidate prints Markdown and performs no network action.
- A pass observed before, or in the same second as, the latest linked failure leaves the bug reproduced and the verified status is refused; a bug with no linked failure cannot be marked verified.
- `--classification blocking` is refused with a hint to use `--scope`, and `--scope product-defect` with a hint to use `--classification`.
- Manual `bug add` and automatic failure capture both name the bug `<date>-<title slug>`, and changing a stored title and then updating its status or evidence leaves the name unchanged.
- Each update appends one Log entry and leaves every earlier Log line, and every body paragraph a person wrote, byte-identical.
- A migrated bug answers to its `BUG-NNNN` alias in list, search, show, update and report, and duplicate and related links resolve from alias to new name and back.
- After the session holding a bug's linked evidence is archived, the bug resolves that evidence to the story's receipt and its verified state is unchanged.
- The CLI documentation says Chough 0.5.x cannot read 0.6.0 bug records.
- `bug update --status fixed-upstream` without a note is refused; with one it closes the bug, `bug list` shows it closed as fixed upstream, and nothing reports it verified.
- A new bug's Steps start with `Trigger:` and the trigger; `bug update --fix <text>` sets the Fix paragraph and logs it; a bug marked verified with no Fix set says which observation passed at which revision instead of `Not fixed yet.`
- A bug added, or updated, with `--observation` naming an evidence entry of the active session is in that session's checkpoint and in its archived story; one naming another session's entry leaves the active checkpoint unchanged.

Validate traceability. The helper SHALL validate observation criterion IDs, requirement IDs and contract paths against their native records before recording. A requirement that the active session's native change adds or modifies in its deltas SHALL count as resolved, as it does for a case run, so evidence can be recorded before `specsync change check` materializes it. `chough evidence add` SHALL require at least one `--criterion`, and `--requirement` and `--contract` SHALL be optional, each validated when given. A refused requirement link SHALL name the companion files and the native change's deltas searched and a likely cause with its fix: the module whose companion holds the ID when it belongs to another module, otherwise a typo. The helper SHALL NOT accept an unresolved link. Trace: LIFE-1, LIFE-2, LIFE-5, FLOW-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- Unknown active HI IDs or absent native requirement IDs are refused; observation IDs cannot overwrite prior observations.
- Observations are unauthenticated claims, including those labelled human or delivery observations.
- A requirement of another module is refused with that module and the fix named; a typo and an unmaterialized delta ID are refused with the check-first hint.
- With a requirement that only the active session's native change adds in its deltas, `chough evidence add --requirement <it>` records; a requirement in neither the companions nor the deltas is refused naming both.
- `chough evidence add` with `--criterion` and no `--requirement` or `--contract` records; without `--criterion` it is refused.

applied_items.content:
SpecSync change steps through Chough. `chough change new <description> [--kind <kind>] [--spec <spec>]... [--path <path>]... [--no-spec-change --rationale <why>]` SHALL run `specsync change new <description>` with the same options and `--json`. `chough change answer <id> <question> <answer>` SHALL run `specsync change answer <id> <question> <answer> --json`. `chough change check <id>` SHALL run `specsync change check <id> --commit`, and `chough change check <id> --no-commit` SHALL run `specsync change check <id>` without it, the check the workflow's accept step runs first to materialize requirement text. `chough change status [<id>]` SHALL run `specsync change status [<id>] --json`. Each SHALL run in the project root given by `--root`, with the `specsync` that Chough's native reads use. Each SHALL pass SpecSync's standard output, standard error and exit code through unchanged, and SHALL write nothing under `.chough/` except the untracked direct-write baseline of REQ-cli-060 under `.chough/local/`. `status` is a read and SHALL keep the native read bound (120 s unless `CHOUGH_NATIVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` sets it); past the bound it SHALL refuse with nothing recorded and name the retry with a longer bound. `new`, `answer` and `check` write, and SHALL never be stopped by that bound. Stopping Chough with SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP SHALL stop the SpecSync process it started (FLOW-14). When `specsync` cannot be started, each SHALL refuse with exit 1 and nothing run, naming the install command from the README's toolchain section and the same step run again.

Acceptance Criteria
- `chough change new --no-spec-change --rationale <why>` passes both options to SpecSync, and `--no-spec-change` without `--rationale` is refused before SpecSync runs, naming the command with `--rationale`.
- Each of `chough change new`, `answer`, `check` and `status` runs SpecSync with exactly the arguments above, in the `--root` directory, and its standard output, standard error and exit code match SpecSync's byte for byte, including a SpecSync refusal's.
- No `chough change` command changes a tracked file under `.chough/`; under `.chough/local/` it changes only its change's direct-write baseline (REQ-cli-060).
- `chough change check` completes after the native read bound has passed, while `chough change status` past the bound refuses with nothing recorded, and the retry it names succeeds.
- When `specsync` cannot be started, each command refuses with exit 1, naming the install command and the step to run again; with SpecSync installed, that step succeeds.
- A SIGTERM to `chough change check` stops the SpecSync process it started.
- `chough change check <id> --no-commit` runs `specsync change check <id>` without `--commit`, passes its output and exit code through, and the next stage move records no `direct-native-write` for what it wrote.

Direct lifecycle writes noted. For the active session's native change, Chough SHALL watch the lifecycle records SpecSync writes in `.specsync/changes/<id>/`: `state.json`, `approvals.json`, `review.json`, `review-attempts.json`, `verification.json` and `verification-attempts.json`. It SHALL keep an untracked baseline of their digests and the change's state in `.chough/local/native-writes/<id>.json`.
- Each `chough change new`, `answer`, `check` and `ship` step SHALL first add any difference from the baseline to the baseline's pending findings, and after its SpecSync step SHALL set the baseline to the records as they are. Chough's own steps are therefore never flagged.
- A successful `chough stage` move, and a successful gate close (REQ-cli-050, REQ-cli-059, REQ-cli-061), SHALL record, before its own event, one `direct-native-write` history event (REQ-history-013) for each pending finding and for any difference from the baseline, so the story reads in the order the writes happened. It SHALL then clear the pending findings and set the baseline.
- Without a baseline, the first writing command SHALL set one and flag nothing.
- `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL show the pending findings and the current difference, as files added, changed or removed, and SHALL write nothing.
- A finding SHALL never refuse a command, and nothing SHALL be recorded outside a stage move or a gate close, so the window between `change check --commit` and finalize gains no write.

Acceptance Criteria
- A lifecycle record changed outside Chough is recorded once, as a `direct-native-write` event naming the file and the state before and after, with the next stage move; a later move records nothing more.
- After `chough change answer` and `chough change check` change the records, the next stage move records no `direct-native-write` event; a write made before such a step is still recorded.
- A project with no baseline records nothing at its first stage move, and a write after that is recorded.
- `chough next` and `chough status` show a pending write with its file, and change no file under `.chough/`.
- A direct write before `chough change ship` is recorded at the move into done that ship makes.
- A lifecycle record changed outside Chough before a review gate closes is recorded before that gate's `gate-closed` entry, not after it; and the workflow's accept steps, run as written, record no `direct-native-write`.

applied_items.content:
Sessions in their own folders. `chough session new <key>` SHALL create `.chough/sessions/<id>/session.md` by create-new, where `<id>` is the date and the slug of `<key>` (REQ-records-003) and `<key>` is kept as an alias, with its own timeline, and SHALL point at it; `session use <id>` SHALL point at an open session by ID, alias or the bare slug when exactly one open session has it; an active pointer that holds such an alias or bare slug, as a 0.5.x pointer that an in-place migration keeps, SHALL name that session, and `chough doctor` SHALL NOT report it as `stale_pointer`; `session list` SHALL report each session's ID, aliases, stage, status (`archived` for an archived story, otherwise its stage status) and whether it is active, open or archived. A session is finished when it is at stage done or its native change is archived on HEAD, at any stage, as the archive's `finalization.json` records, read without a native read (DRIVE-16). A session SHALL close only itself, at its own move into done or with `chough session close --reason`: `session new` and `session use` SHALL NOT archive, close or change any other session, even a finished one (#207, #214). `session list`, `chough next` and `chough doctor` SHALL list each finished open session with its fix, `chough doctor --fix` (REQ-history-012), which keeps one with unfolded inbox entries or an open awaiting-human gate open and names the recovery: `chough inbox fold`, or `chough checkpoint --close-gate`, since closing a gate is a decision (#181). When `chough stage advance` moves the active session into done and its save succeeds, after the knowledge refresh of REQ-cli-043, the helper SHALL archive that session in the same command and clear the active pointer, reporting `applied.session_archive` with status `archived` and the ID; a session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL stay open with its pointer, reported as `kept_open` with the count; a session for which release is authorized at that move (a run consent or a standing preference, as `stage enter release` requires) SHALL stay open for the release, reported as `kept_open` with that reason, and SHALL archive itself the same way at the move from release into done. The step SHALL NOT undo the move into done. To archive a session, Chough SHALL write `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md` by create-new: the session's front matter with `stage: done` (or the stage it closed at), `stage_status: archived`, no `next`, since the session's next action no longer applies, `closed` (the UTC date) and `outcome` (`done` or `closed-without-done`), and `receipts`, one map per evidence entry the session holds, ordered by its observation time, oldest first, then by ID, with its `id`, `aliases` (one scalar, comma-and-space separated), `claim`, `result`, `observed` (the entry's observation time, ISO UTC, REQ-cli-017), `duration_seconds` (the run's wall-clock seconds, when known), `command`, `revision`, `environment`, `content`, `fingerprint`, `raw_log` when present, `case`, `case_digest`, `screenshot` when present and `actor` when known (REQ-records-007), so a bug whose evidence is archived keeps its verified state, which needs a pass observed after its latest failure (REQ-cli-012), and the timing report can order and time case runs read from receipts (REQ-reporting-001); then the story as written, whose What was verified SHALL give the latest receipt of each case and every receipt bound to no case, one line each (its claim, its command unless the claim already holds it, and the first 12 digits of its fingerprint, ending `^<evidence id>`) for each entry not already listed, with one line counting the earlier runs of those cases, which stay in `receipts`, the Timeline and a closing line `Closed <date>: <outcome>.` Chough SHALL read the story back and compare it before it removes anything, and SHALL then remove the session folder, `session.md`, `evidence/` and `agent/` included, and move its screenshots beside the story (REQ-records-013), each file only under REQ-records-012; files it keeps SHALL be reported, the folder SHALL count as archived while its story exists, and `chough doctor --fix` SHALL finish the removal once they are committed. Archiving a session SHALL NOT read, move, rewrite or remove any other session's folder or story. After it, `next` and `status` SHALL refuse with "no open session" and name `chough session new <key>` until a session is opened (DRIVE-13). Evidence and bug links into an archived session SHALL resolve to its story's receipts. Two branches that record work in different sessions SHALL merge without conflict. A session that cannot be read, because it is over the bound of REQ-records-001 or invalid, SHALL NOT stop `session list`, `session new`, `session use` or another session's `next`; `session list` SHALL report it with the reason and the recovery `chough session shelve <id>`, which SHALL move the folder unparsed and byte for byte to `.chough/archive/shelved/<id>/` with a `shelved.md` giving its size, SHA-256 per file, time and reason, and clear the active pointer when it named that session. Shelving SHALL never replace a file, and no reader SHALL scan `.chough/archive/shelved/` (DRIVE-14). `chough session close <id> --reason <text>` SHALL close an open session for abandoned work without a native read: it SHALL refuse with nothing changed a blank reason, a session that is archived or does not exist, and a session with unfolded inbox entries, naming `chough session use <id>` and `chough inbox fold`; otherwise it SHALL add the decision `Closed without done: <reason>` and archive the session as above with outcome `closed-without-done`, clearing the active pointer when it named that session (DRIVE-16). Trace: DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24, DRIVE-25, KNOW-30, KNOW-34, LIFE-3, LIFE-7, DRIVE-14, DRIVE-13, DRIVE-16.

Acceptance Criteria
- Two branches that each advance a different session merge in Git with no conflict and keep both sessions' timelines.
- The move into done of the active session writes `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md` with every receipt and the full timeline, removes the committed session folder, clears the pointer, reports `archived`, and `next` then refuses naming `chough session new <key>`.
- Each receipt in the story gives its entry's `observed` time, its `duration_seconds`, `raw_log` and `actor` when the entry has them, and its `aliases` as one comma-and-space separated scalar; a bug whose linked pass was observed after its latest linked failure stays verified once that session is archived.
- Regression for issue 165: with seven earlier archived stories present, among them 0.5.x-era stories, and `knowledge/` neither tracked nor ignored, advancing accept to done leaves every earlier story byte-identical in place, `git status` shows no deleted file, and the only new committed record is the new story; the same path in the 0.5.x layout is recorded failing first on the 0.5.0 code and linked to a local bug.
- With an uncommitted file in `agent/`, the move into done writes the story, keeps that file and its folder, reports it, and `next` does not treat the folder as open; after a commit, `doctor --fix` removes the folder.
- At the move into done, a session with unfolded inbox entries stays open (`kept_open` with the count).
- Regression for #207: with a finished session whose native change is archived and that still waits on a publish gate, `session new` and `session use` leave it byte-identical and open, and `next` and `doctor` list it as finished with its fix.
- With release authorized before the move into done, the session stays open (`kept_open`), `stage enter release` works, and the move from release into done archives it.
- A session whose native change is archived on HEAD, at a stage short of done, is listed as finished with no native read, and only `chough doctor --fix` archives it.
- `session list` reports open, active and archived sessions; `session use` accepts the ID, the alias and a unique bare slug.
- With one session over its bound and another unreadable, `session list` reports each with `chough session shelve <id>`, and `next` on the active session and `session new` still work; shelving moves the folder byte for byte under `.chough/archive/shelved/`.
- `chough session close <id> --reason <text>` archives the session with outcome `closed-without-done` and the reason in its decisions; a blank reason, an archived or missing session and a session with unfolded inbox entries refuse with nothing changed.
- After an in-place migration whose machine-local pointer holds a 0.5.x session key, `next` and `status` read that session, and `chough doctor` reports no `stale_pointer`.
- A story's receipts, and its What was verified lines for them, are in observation-time order, oldest first, whatever order the session referenced them in.
- A session with three runs of one case and one manual entry archives a story whose What was verified lists the case's latest run and the manual entry, each command once, and a line counting 2 earlier runs, while `receipts` keeps all four.
- An archived story's front matter gives `stage_status: archived` and no `next`.

applied_items.content:
Append-only timeline. Each session's transitions SHALL be recorded as entries of the `## Timeline` section of its `session.md` (REQ-records-004), and those entries, carried into the archived story at finish, SHALL be the session's only transition history: no event file, cycle directory, cursor or transitions log SHALL be written. Each entry SHALL be one list item, `- <time> · <kind> · <from> → <to> · <text> ^<entry id>`, where `<time>` is the UTC time to the second in ISO 8601, `<kind>` is a transition kind (`start`, `advance`, `iterate`, `back`, `reset`, `pause`, `resume`, `skip`, `enter`, `return`, `gate-opened`, `gate-closed`, `direct-native-write`, `correction`), `<text>` is the reason, gate or note, and `<entry id>` is `t-` and 6 lowercase hexadecimal digits from fresh random bits, unique in the file. Its structured fields SHALL follow as indented `- <key>: <value>` lines, plain text and never JSON: a field with parts, such as `relayed_by` and `direct_write`, SHALL be a `- <key>:` line with one `- <part>: <value>` line per part indented under it, and a list of parts one level further; a value that holds a line break, or starts or ends with a space or a `"`, SHALL be written as a JSON string, and Chough SHALL still read the JSON value of an entry written before this rule. The fields are `by` for the actor (REQ-records-007), `native_change` when one is recorded, and the fields of REQ-history-005, REQ-history-010, REQ-history-013, REQ-history-014 and REQ-history-015. `chough init` and `chough session new` SHALL each append one `start` entry, whose `<from>` and `<to>` are the stage the session starts in and whose text is its objective or key, and `chough timing` SHALL read it as the start of that stage's first segment. The entry and the checkpoint change it goes with SHALL be written in the same atomic replace of `session.md`, so a refused or failed save leaves neither. Chough SHALL only append entries: it SHALL never edit, reorder or remove an existing entry line, and an entry ID SHALL never be reused in its file. A timeline entry is what other requirements call a transition, and the session file's Timeline is what they call its transition log. `chough doctor` SHALL report a session or story whose Timeline at HEAD is not an exact prefix of its Timeline in the working tree (REQ-history-012). Trace: LIFE-2, LIFE-3, LIFE-6, LIFE-7, FLOW-2, FLOW-13, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24.

Acceptance Criteria
- Every transition kind written in a fixture session appears once, in order, as an entry with its time, kind, stages, text, unique entry ID and structured fields, and no file is written under `.chough/history/` or `.chough/transitions.jsonl`.
- A save refused after its native read leaves `session.md` byte-identical, with no entry and no checkpoint change.
- Two branches that each advance a different session merge with no conflict and keep both timelines.
- Editing an earlier entry by hand and committing nothing else makes `chough doctor` report the session's timeline as rewritten.
- Each session's timeline holds only its own entries, and a stage move in one session leaves every other session's file unchanged.
- A gate closed with a relayed decision and a direct lifecycle write each add an entry whose `relayed_by` and `direct_write` parts are labelled lines with no JSON object, and `history show`, `timing` and `doctor` read both those entries and entries written with JSON values.
- `chough init` and `chough session new` each write one `start` entry, and `chough timing` right after reports the intent segment as started at that entry's time, not unknown.

applied_items.content:
Doctor findings and fixes. `chough doctor` (REQ-cli-055) SHALL find this debt without a native read, and its fixes SHALL use Chough's own steps:
- `unmigrated`: a 0.5.x record (REQ-records-010). The fix SHALL name `chough migrate` and SHALL NOT migrate.
- `leak`: a committed record that matches REQ-records-006, with its file, line and kind and never the text. The fix SHALL name `chough doctor --fix --redact`, which SHALL redact the matches in place and is not a decision.
- `stale_pointer`: the active pointer names a session that is missing or archived. The fix SHALL remove the pointer.
- `finished_session`: an open session that is finished (REQ-history-006) and has no open awaiting-human gate. The fix SHALL archive it. A session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL instead be `skipped`, naming `chough inbox fold`.
- `unfinished_archive`: a session folder whose story exists and that still holds files. The fix SHALL remove each file whose bytes are committed at HEAD (REQ-records-012) and report the rest as `skipped`, naming the commit to make.
- `stale_gates`: an open session whose native change is archived on HEAD and that has open awaiting-human gates. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL withdraw those gates as `chough checkpoint --clear-awaiting-human` does, recording no human decision, and SHALL then archive the session as the `finished_session` fix does.
- `unfinished_session`: an open, unfinished session named with `--close <id>`. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL close the session as `chough session close <id> --reason` does.
- `timeline_rewritten`: a session or story whose Timeline at HEAD is not an exact prefix of its working Timeline (REQ-history-002). It has no fix; the finding names the entries that differ.
- `alias_conflict`: an ID that is the `id` or alias of two records (REQ-records-003). It has no fix; the finding names both records.
- `oversize`: a committed record, evidence entry or screenshot over its bound (REQ-records-001, REQ-records-005, REQ-records-013). It has no fix; the finding names the file, its size and the bound, and the verify lane's `leaks` step fails on it as it does on `leak`, so CI refuses an oversized receipt.
- `unreadable`: a committed Chough record under `.chough/` that its reader refuses, such as front matter outside the subset of REQ-records-001, which makes `chough status` and `chough next` refuse the project. It has no fix; the finding names the file and the reader's reason with its line, and names `chough session shelve <id>` for an open session's `session.md`. A record over its bound is `oversize` instead.
- `records_in_verification`: `.specsync/sdd.json` exists and its `verification_ignored_paths` lacks one of Chough's record folders (REQ-records-014). It has no fix, because Chough never writes SpecSync's policy; the finding names the entries to add.
- `merge_drivers`: in a Git work tree, a clone whose Git config has no command for `merge.chough-bug.driver` or `merge.chough-generated.driver` (a fresh clone has neither), or whose `.gitattributes` lacks one of the merge lines of REQ-cli-047. It is one finding, naming the missing drivers and lines. The fix SHALL set the missing drivers in the clone's local Git config and SHALL NOT write `.gitattributes`, a committed file a person reviews. A missing line SHALL leave the finding `skipped`, naming the lines to add and `chough init`, which appends exactly those.
- `merge_driver_outdated`: the merge drivers are set, and the `chough` they run, found through `PATH` as Git finds it, is missing or reports a version older than the running Chough, so a merge would run older code on these records. It has no fix; the finding names both versions and the install command from the README's toolchain section.

- `stale_pointer`: the active pointer names a session that is missing or archived. The fix SHALL remove the pointer.
- `finished_session`: an open session that is finished (REQ-history-006) and has no open awaiting-human gate. The fix SHALL archive it. A session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL instead be `skipped`, naming `chough inbox fold`.
- `unfinished_archive`: a session folder whose story exists and that still holds files. The fix SHALL remove each file whose bytes are committed at HEAD (REQ-records-012) and report the rest as `skipped`, naming the commit to make.
- `stale_gates`: an open session whose native change is archived on HEAD and that has open awaiting-human gates. This fix is a decision. - `alias_conflict`: an ID that is the `id` or alias of two records (REQ-records-003). It has no fix; the finding names both records.

Migration from 0.5.x. `chough migrate` SHALL read a project's 0.5.x records, write nothing, and print the plan: each 0.5.x file with its SHA-256 and what it becomes, each 0.6.0 file it would write, every value it would redact by kind (REQ-records-006), and every file it would remove without carrying it, with why, and SHALL end with the plan's SHA-256; while any native change in the project is not archived, the preview SHALL also say that `--apply` will refuse until it is, naming each such change. `chough migrate --apply <plan digest>` SHALL refuse, writing nothing, unless the plan it builds has that digest, so nothing is migrated that was not previewed first; it SHALL also refuse, writing nothing, while any native change in the project is not archived, naming each, so it never runs while a change is open, and unless the human's consent is given, either as `--consent <source>` naming who consented, their words and where, which the receipt records as a relayed claim, or as a standing `migration` preference with its source (REQ-cli-013), and Chough SHALL NOT infer consent from the digest or from any other record; it SHALL also refuse, writing nothing, while a 0.5.x file to be removed differs from its bytes at HEAD or is untracked, naming each, so Git holds every byte it removes. It SHALL then write the 0.6.0 tree by create-new only and SHALL refuse, writing nothing more, when a file it would write already exists with other bytes; it SHALL read each written file back and compare its digest; it SHALL write the receipt `.chough/archive/migrations/<YYYY-MM-DD>-from-0-5.md` listing, for every file before and after, its path, size and SHA-256, the redactions by file, field and kind, every removed file with why and the commit that holds it, and the old-to-new ID map, with `none` under any of its sections that has nothing to list; and only then SHALL it remove the 0.5.x files, each only when its bytes still match the plan. It SHALL never weaken a SpecSync archive: before removing anything it SHALL read the native validity of every archived change whose acceptance manifest lists a file it would remove, at most 8 reads at once, read them again after the removal, and, if any archive that read valid no longer does, restore every removed file byte for byte and refuse, naming those archives. A file written by an interrupted apply with the planned bytes SHALL count as done on the next apply, and a second apply on a migrated tree SHALL report nothing to do; on a tree with no 0.5.x record the preview SHALL likewise say there is nothing to migrate and give no plan digest. The mapping SHALL be: each open session, legacy `.chough/session.json` included, becomes a session folder whose timeline holds, in order, every transition of its selected history lineage, the legacy log's entries going to the session that adopted them; each archived session, and each session rolled into `knowledge/attachments/`, becomes an archived story; each observation an open session references becomes an evidence entry of that session, each one an archived session or a bug references becomes a receipt of that story or bug, and others are removed; a PNG or JPEG artifact of a carried observation that fits the bounds of REQ-records-013 is kept beside its session or story, and other artifacts are removed; each bug becomes a Markdown bug; inbox entries move to their session's `agent/inbox/`; every 0.5.x ID is kept as an alias (REQ-records-003), and an ID whose record was removed without being carried SHALL resolve as `removed`, naming the receipt, never as current or passed; and `.chough/transitions.jsonl`, `.chough/history/`, `.chough/pruned.jsonl`, `.chough/session.v1.json`, `.chough/artifacts/` other than files an open bug names, shelved 0.5.x sessions and the generated or copied vault content of REQ-cli-044 are removed after they are listed. Every file migration writes SHALL pass REQ-records-006 with redaction, so no home-folder path, user name or credential survives in a rewritten record; a file it keeps byte for byte (an open bug's fixture, a `library/` snapshot or brief) that matches SHALL be listed in the plan and the receipt as a `leak` finding for a person to fix, never changed silently and never kept unreported. The receipt SHALL say that Git history still holds what earlier commits leaked, which this migration does not rewrite. Case definitions and preferences SHALL stay byte-identical. Removal SHALL follow REQ-records-012. Trace: DRIVE-27, LIFE-20, LIFE-21, LIFE-8, KNOW-10, KNOW-11, KNOW-30, KNOW-31, KNOW-34, LIFE-26.

Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures captured from a project at every released 0.x version, 0.1.0 to 0.5.0, each built from its release tag, migrate to the same kind of 0.6.0 tree with every record readable (#213).
- `--apply` without a digest, or with the digest of an earlier plan, refuses and writes nothing; `--apply` with the preview's digest proceeds.
- With a native change that is not archived, or with neither `--consent` nor a standing `migration` preference, `--apply` with the preview's digest refuses and writes nothing, naming the open change or the missing consent; with consent the receipt records its source.
- With a SpecSync stub whose archive reads invalid once a listed file is gone, `--apply` restores every removed file byte for byte and refuses naming that archive.
- A rewritten record that held a home-folder path holds `<redacted:home-path>` and the receipt counts it; a kept fixture holding one is listed as a `leak` finding and left unchanged; the receipt says Git history is not rewritten.
- On a 0.5.x fixture with a legacy checkpoint, adopted history, two open and seven archived sessions, rolled sessions in the vault, a bug of each ID form, inbox entries and old proof, `chough migrate` writes nothing and lists every file, target, redaction and removal.
- `--apply` with an uncommitted or untracked 0.5.x file refuses naming it, with nothing written.
- `--apply` writes every planned file and the receipt, removes the 0.5.x files, and afterwards every record, alias and timeline entry is readable by `next`, `status`, `bug show`, `session list` and `timing`; the receipt's before and after digests match the files at the earlier and the new commit.
- With a target that already exists with other bytes, `--apply` refuses and writes nothing more; after an apply interrupted between writes, the next apply completes and the result equals an uninterrupted one; a second apply on the result reports nothing to do.
- Case definition files and `.chough/preferences.json` are byte-identical before and after.
- Every transition of the selected lineage appears once, in order, in its session's timeline, and every archived session, the rolled ones included, is an archived story.
- A bug linking an observation that was removed without being carried shows it as `removed` with the receipt named, and `chough next` never counts it as current or passed.
- Regression for the local bug where history writes refused once the adopting session rolled into the vault: a 0.5.x fixture whose adopting session sits in `knowledge/attachments/`, with `.chough/transitions.jsonl` unchanged, migrates; the legacy entries land in that session's archived story, and afterwards `checkpoint --awaiting-human`, `--close-gate` and a stage move all succeed. The same writes are first recorded refusing on the last build before #142 (90e5de6f^), with the same tree recorded as observed on 0.5.0.
- With a native change open, the preview names it and says `--apply` will refuse, and writes nothing; the apply then refuses with `refused:change-open`.
- A migration with no redaction, no kept leak and nothing left uncarried writes a receipt whose Redactions, Kept with leaks and Not carried sections each say `none`.
- On a migrated tree, `chough migrate` says there is nothing to migrate and prints no plan digest, and writes nothing.

applied_items.content:
Journal and feed. The knowledge vault's journal SHALL be dated Markdown posts in `knowledge/journal/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`, each with front matter giving `id`, `title`, `type: journal`, `tags`, `date`, `time` (the UTC time it was written, ISO 8601 to the second; the file name keeps only the date), `kind` (`shipped`, `closed`, `intent`, `spec`, `broke` or `learned`), `links` and, for a finished session, `record`, the path of its archived story. `chough checkpoint --title <title>` SHALL record the session's post title, one line of at most 72 bytes, as `title`, and `chough checkpoint --summary <text>` its post summary of at most 900 bytes as `summary`, one list item per non-blank line of the text; each SHALL replace the earlier value, an empty value SHALL remove it, both SHALL pass REQ-records-006, and the story SHALL keep both, so the agent who did the work writes the post's short human title and its summary before the move into done. When a session archives itself at its move into done (REQ-history-006), Chough SHALL write a `shipped` post, or a `closed` post for a session closed without done, by create-new. Its title SHALL be the session's `title`, or, when it has none, a title derived from its objective: the text before the first `: `, `; `, `, `, ` (` or ` — ` that starts at least 16 bytes in, cut at a word to at most 72 bytes and ending in `…` when cut. Its body SHALL be the session's `summary`, one paragraph per line, or, when it has none, a body derived from the story: the Goal's first paragraph, then `Why:` with the first Decisions and why entry, then `Verified:` with the newest What was verified entry, then `Next:` with the first Open threads entry, an empty part left out. The body SHALL be cut at a sentence end so that it stays within 1,200 bytes with the line that follows it, a line linking the PR when the session names one, the archived story and, when the session's native change is archived, its `.specsync/archive/changes/` folder, so the post is short and the story holds the full record. `chough journal add --record <story> --title <title> --body <text> [--link <link>]...` SHALL write the post of an archived story that has none, for a backfill of stories archived before the journal began or before this rule: its `kind` SHALL be `shipped` when the story's `outcome` is `done` and `closed` otherwise, its `date` the story's `closed` date, its `time` the latest time among the story's Timeline entries when that time falls on that date (otherwise it records none), its `record` the story, and its links those of the post at the move into done followed by each `--link`; it SHALL refuse, writing nothing, when the story does not exist or when a post's `record` already names it, naming that post. The journal and its feed SHALL be the timeline of archived changes: `knowledge/index.md` SHALL present them as that timeline and SHALL link `.specsync/archive/changes/` for changes archived before the journal began (REQ-cli-043), and no other timeline page SHALL be generated. `chough journal add --kind <kind> --title <title> --body <text> [--link <link>]...` SHALL write any other post by create-new, refusing a body over 1,200 bytes. Chough SHALL never rewrite or remove a post, so a person's edit is kept. `knowledge/journal/feed.xml` SHALL be an Atom feed of the newest 20 posts, newest first by `time`. A post without a `time`, such as a migrated or hand-written one, SHALL sort by its date and then its name, after the timed posts of the same date, and the index SHALL mark it "(no time)". The index's newest 10 posts SHALL use the same order. An entry's `<updated>` SHALL be its `time` when it has one, and the feed's `<updated>` the first entry's. The feed SHALL be generated from the posts with identical bytes for the same posts, and `chough library index` SHALL regenerate it, with `--check` covering it (REQ-cli-047). The journal SHALL copy no record: it links them. Trace: KNOW-33, KNOW-30, KNOW-31, KNOW-15, KNOW-4, KNOW-14.

Acceptance Criteria
- The move into done of a session with a PR and an archived native change writes one `shipped` post whose body is at most 1,200 bytes and links the PR, `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md` and the change's archive folder, and `feed.xml` lists it.
- `knowledge/index.md` names the journal and feed as the timeline of archived changes and links `.specsync/archive/changes/`, and no `timeline.md` or `timeline/` is generated.
- A person's edit to a post survives a later move into done and `library index`, and a post name that already exists is never overwritten.
- `chough journal add` writes a post of each kind, and a body over 1,200 bytes is refused with nothing written.
- Regenerating `feed.xml` twice gives identical bytes, it parses as XML, and `library index --check` fails naming it after a hand edit.
- Each new post records `time`. Posts written on one day are listed newest first in the index and the feed, a post without a `time` follows that day's timed posts and is marked "(no time)" in the index, and an entry's `<updated>` is its `time`.
- With `chough checkpoint --title` and `--summary` set, the move into done writes a post whose title is that title and whose body holds each summary line; without them, the title is the objective's first clause within 72 bytes and the body holds the Goal, the first decision, the newest verified entry and the first open thread, within 1,200 bytes with its links.
- `chough checkpoint --title` over 72 bytes or holding a line break, and `--summary` over 900 bytes, are refused with nothing written; an empty value removes the field.
- `chough journal add --record <story>` writes one post dated by the story's `closed`, with the story's latest Timeline time on that date, its `record` and links, of kind `shipped` for a done story and `closed` otherwise; a second `--record` for the same story, or one naming no archived story, is refused with nothing written.

No leaks in committed records. Before writing any committed record, Chough SHALL check every value it writes, in front matter and body, including recorded commands, summaries, reasons, decisions, relayed words and places, notes, limitations, titles and actor values, for: an absolute path under a home, temporary or system root (`/Users/`, `/home/`, `/root/`, `/private/`, `/tmp/`, `/var/`, `/Volumes/`, `/mnt/`) or a Windows drive path; a `~/` path; the local host name, and the local user name when it appears inside a path or as `<user>@<host>`; an email address; and credentials: GitHub, GitLab, Slack, AWS and model-provider token forms, private key blocks, bearer and basic authorization values, JSON web tokens, and `password`, `secret`, `token` or `api_key` assignments with a value of 8 or more characters. A value that matches SHALL refuse the write as `refused:leak`, naming the field and the kind of match and never the matched text, with every file byte-identical. With `--redact`, each match SHALL instead be replaced by `<redacted:<kind>>` and the write SHALL proceed, saying how many values were redacted. A human's configured display name (REQ-records-008) SHALL NOT count as a user name. `chough doctor` SHALL scan every file Git tracks under `.chough/` and `knowledge/` for the same patterns and SHALL report each as a `leak` finding with the file, the line and the kind, never the text, except that a path under `/tmp/` or `/private/tmp/` in a case definition (`.chough/cases/*.cases.toml`) is a deliberate test setting, such as a case's own `XDG_DATA_HOME`, and SHALL NOT be reported or offered `--redact`, while a home path, the local user or host name, an email or a credential in a case definition still SHALL; the verify and CI lanes SHALL run that scan and fail on a finding. Trace: LIFE-26, LIFE-17, FLOW-22.

Acceptance Criteria
- Each pattern kind, placed in an evidence summary, a decision, a relayed `--words`, a bug note and a recorded command, refuses the write with `refused:leak` naming the field and kind, the output never contains the matched text, and every file is unchanged.
- The same writes with `--redact` store `<redacted:<kind>>` and report the count.
- A decision naming the configured human display name is written; the same name inside `/Users/<name>/` is refused.
- With one committed record holding a home path, `chough doctor` reports a `leak` finding with its file, line and kind, without the path, and exits 1; `fledge lanes run verify` fails on it.
- The records of a full fixture cycle run inside a temporary directory hold no absolute path, user name or host name.
- A committed case definition whose binding sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` to a path under `/tmp/` gives no `leak` finding from `chough doctor`, while one holding a home-folder path still gives one naming the file and line.

applied_items.content:
A human's gate approval drives the native approval as that human. Chough SHALL read human identities from configuration, never from its source: the user configuration file `chough/identity.toml` under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (by default `~/.config`), overridden by `.chough/local/identity.toml` when present, each `[[human]]` giving `name`, the display name records show, optional `aliases`, and `specsync_actor`, the actor SpecSync records. Every close of a gate with a human's decision (REQ-cli-050, REQ-cli-059, REQ-cli-061), whatever the gate drives and with or without `--no-native`, SHALL resolve `--decided-by` to one configured human by name or alias before anything runs or is written. When the gate drives a native step (REQ-cli-030), Chough SHALL then run, before it records anything, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <specsync_actor> --note <note>` for a gate that drives approval, the note giving the human's exact words, where and when they decided, and the agent that relayed or recorded it, or `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <specsync_actor> --verdict <pass or block>` for one that drives review, with the verdict given as `--verdict` on the close, which SHALL be required there and SHALL never be read from the words. A human decision that is neither an approval nor a review, such as a request for changes, SHALL be recorded with `--no-native`, which closes the gate with the relay and runs nothing; Chough SHALL NOT decide which case applies from the words. When SpecSync refuses, Chough SHALL pass its output and exit code through and record nothing; when it succeeds, Chough SHALL close the gate with the relay and add the decision, which SHALL name the native step run. `--decided-by` naming no configured human, or two, SHALL be refused as `refused:human-identity-unknown`, naming both configuration files and the keys to add, before anything runs; Chough SHALL NOT guess an identity or fall back to an agent account. A gate that drives no native step SHALL run no native step, and its decision is still in the configured human's name. An agent that approves or reviews on authority the human gave in advance, without the human answering that gate, SHALL record the native step as the acting agent, `<agent>-<terminal>` (REQ-cli-029), quoting the human's earlier words and where they said them, so only a decision made at that gate is in the human's name (FLOW-24). No source file, skill, template or document SHALL name a specific person as the default human. The relay remains an unauthenticated claim (FLOW-16). Trace: FLOW-23, FLOW-24, FLOW-16, FLOW-10, LIFE-26.

Acceptance Criteria
- With a configured human and a scope gate that drives approval, closing it with that human's relay runs `specsync change approve` once with the configured actor and a note holding the words, place and relaying agent, then closes the gate and records the decision.
- The same at an acceptance gate with `--verdict pass` runs `specsync change review --reviewer` as that human with that verdict, and without `--verdict` it refuses before anything runs; `--no-native` closes a driving gate with the relay and starts no SpecSync process.
- A SpecSync refusal's output and exit code pass through, the gate stays open and nothing is written.
- An unconfigured or ambiguous `--decided-by` refuses with `refused:human-identity-unknown` naming both files, and no SpecSync process starts.
- `.chough/local/identity.toml` overrides the user file; a gate that drives nothing closes with no native call.
- An approval or review on authority given in advance names the agent account `<agent>-<terminal>` as the SpecSync actor and quotes the human's earlier words and place, and never the human as the actor.
- A search of `src/`, `skills/`, `docs/` and `README.md` finds no person's name or account given as a default identity.
- With no identity file, or one that does not name `--decided-by`, closing an intent gate that drives nothing, closing a driving gate with `--no-native`, and the same through `chough gate record` and `chough change ship --close-gate`, each refuse with `refused:human-identity-unknown` before anything runs, with every file unchanged; for a configured human each succeeds.

applied_items.content:
Gate lists. `chough gate list [--json]` SHALL number every open human gate of every open session in the project from 1, with the stage it holds and the native step it drives (REQ-cli-030). It SHALL give each a one-screen summary of at most 24 lines and 4,096 bytes, with:
- what changed: the files, insertions and deletions since the change's base, leaving out `.chough/`, the knowledge directory and SpecSync lifecycle bookkeeping, and naming the five files with the most changed lines among the rest (#190). At a gate that drives approval, the change's own definition, the Markdown files under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` (its `change.md`, deltas, plan and other artifacts), is what the human approves, so the summary SHALL count those files and name them first, its deltas before the change's other files with the requirement IDs each delta adds or modifies, never leaving them out as bookkeeping. At a gate held at intent, the summary SHALL give the intent being approved in place of what changed when the session records no native change: the criterion IDs the session references and the HI files that hold them. The base is the change's own `base_commit` (from its `state.json`), so an earlier change on the same branch is not counted again. The base is instead the merge base of HEAD with the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `main`) in two cases: when that merge base is not an ancestor of the `base_commit`, meaning default-branch work was merged or rebased in after the change began (#190), and when the change records no `base_commit`. A merge base that is HEAD itself, as on the default branch, is not used. With no usable base, the summary says the base is unknown;
- the tests: how many cases passed, failed and were not run, by the latest observation of each case that links a requirement the change's deltas add or modify, or that the session's observations name, with the failing case IDs;
- the risks: the first 8 lines of the change's `plan.md` section "Risks", or "none recorded";
- a diff link: the GitHub compare URL from the base to HEAD when `origin` is a GitHub remote, otherwise `git diff <base>..<HEAD>`.

Each summary's digest SHALL be the SHA-256 of its text. The list SHALL be saved as `.chough/local/gate-lists/<list>.json`, where `<list>` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the list. Listing SHALL make no native read and write no tracked file. The list SHALL end with how to reply: `chough gate record` for the gates whose change is not verifying, and `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for each gate whose change is verifying.

`chough gate record <list> --gates <n>[,<n>...] --decided-by <who> --words <words> --where <where> --recorded-by <agent>` SHALL close each named gate as `chough checkpoint --close-gate` would with the four values (REQ-cli-050), and its relay SHALL carry that gate's `summary_digest` and the `list` (REQ-history-014). It SHALL close all the named gates or none. Before writing anything, it SHALL refuse:
- an unknown list, a number not on it, a listed gate that is no longer open, or a gate whose summary's digest has changed, each naming `chough gate list`;
- a gate whose change's `state.json` state is `verifying`, naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` with the relay, and giving as the reason that such a gate closes through the ship, which runs the review as the human and closes the gate after the native ship, never that Chough's records may not be written;
- more than one named gate that drives a native step, naming the gates to record one at a time.

A named gate that drives a native step SHALL run it as the decided human (REQ-records-008) before any gate is closed.

Acceptance Criteria
- `gate list` numbers each open gate with a summary naming what changed, the tests, the risks and a diff link, at most 24 lines, and the SHA-256 digest of its text; the list is saved under `.chough/local/gate-lists/` and no tracked file changes.
- One `gate record` reply naming two listed gates closes both, each relay keeping the same words and its own summary digest; a gate left off the reply stays open.
- An unknown list, a number not listed, a gate no longer open and a summary changed since listing are each refused with nothing written, and listing again then recording succeeds.
- A gate whose change is verifying is refused, naming `chough change ship` with `--list` and `--gate`, which then ships and closes it with its digest.
- Two named gates that both drive a native step are refused with nothing run or written; one such gate with gates that drive nothing runs its step once and closes all of them.
- #190: with a one-line product edit, 300 changed records under `.chough/` and `knowledge/`, and 200 files merged from main after the base, the summary counts one file and names it.
- For a second native change on one branch, the summary's what changed counts only that change's own files since its `base_commit`, not the earlier change's; with default-branch work merged in after it began, it counts from the merge base, as #190's criterion requires.
- At a scope gate, the summary's what changed counts and names the change's deltas and plan under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` first, while its `state.json` and `approvals.json` stay left out.
- With a verifying change's review gate open, `gate list` ends naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for it and offers no `gate record` for it, and the `gate record` refusal gives the ship as its reason, with no claim that Chough's records may not be written.
- At a scope gate whose change has more than five Markdown files, the summary names the delta and the requirement IDs it adds or modifies before the other files.
- At an intent gate with no native change recorded, the summary names the session's criterion IDs and their HI files instead of an unknown base.

applied_items.content:
Focused next action. `chough next` SHALL print a compact action view, separate from the full `chough status` report: the objective; the current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers; the recorded native change with its read state, summary state, approval and correction validity, terminal evidence validity, native next action and approved-delta result; the next valid action with its reason and, when one applies, its command; the gate for the next main stage; awaiting-human gates; blockers; the checkpoint's open questions; open acceptance-blocking bug IDs with the count of other open bugs; only the referenced observations that need attention, each once: those that are not current, leaving out a superseded run, an earlier run of a case whose later run the checkpoint also references, with counts for the rest, superseded runs counted apart; the most recent checkpoint decisions, at most 5 with their total, showing the kind and reason of entries that follow the `decided:`, `rejected:` or `failed:` prefix convention and other entries whole; the latest failed observation by its recorded observation time, with the status of each bug that links it; and a pointer to each module's native lesson source with the count and bounded paths of archived SpecSync lesson bundles, without reading lesson text or tracking which bundles were folded; the bundles named SHALL be the newest 3 by recorded finalization timestamp, then directory, with an unreadable timestamp sorting oldest, the same 3 that `knowledge/index.md` links (REQ-cli-043). `chough status` SHALL report the same open questions, all of them, in its checkpoint section. It SHALL print text by default and the same fields as JSON with `--json`, and each form SHALL be at most 16384 bytes, with every list bounded, its total stated and any truncation marked. The same records SHALL give byte-identical output; ordering SHALL use recorded fields and names, never file modification times. At plan, while the native change waits for its definition approval, the next valid action SHALL name the human scope gate, opened with `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>" --drives approve` when none is open and closed with `chough checkpoint --close-gate` and the human's decision, and neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`, so no agent is routed to approve its own scope; an approval on authority the human gave in advance stays as REQ-cli-029 describes. Likewise at accept, neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action for the review, `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <name>`, in any field, the native summary and the gate to done included, so no agent is routed to review its own work; where they show SpecSync's next action there, it SHALL read as the human's review at the review gate. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL derive the next valid action from the same rules and SHALL each make at most one native status read. The move into done archives the session (REQ-history-006), after which `chough next` refuses with "no open session" and names `chough session new <key>`. A session stays open at done only while an authorized release is still ahead or unfolded inbox entries keep it open; then, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action SHALL name, release first, `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, since the session archives itself only at the move from release into done; otherwise, while inbox entries are unfolded, including after that move, it SHALL name `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`. It SHALL do so rather than repeat the checkpoint's next action, and SHALL NOT recommend a stage reset. A stage reset SHALL replace the checkpoint's next action. In an earlier main stage, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence and no pause, human gate or blocking bug applies, the next valid action SHALL NOT continue the stage; it SHALL say the change is archived and recommend the new cycle, a stage reset that carries a reason followed by a new native change, except at accept, where it SHALL recommend recording done first, with `chough stage advance`, which archives the session. An archived change finalized no later than the latest reset, or reached directly by one, is the previous cycle's: before done the action SHALL keep the reset's guidance and, when the next gate is refused, name `specsync change new`, never the archived refusal or another reset. With no native change recorded, a refused `refused:no-native-change` gate SHALL name `specsync change new`, not a bare status read. The next valid action SHALL guide a fresh agent through every stage (#76): right after `chough init` at intent with no criteria referenced, it SHALL say to capture or read the intent and name `hi check`, then `chough context`; at test, it SHALL name `chough cases select` and `chough cases run` for the selected cases, and `chough bug add` for a referenced case whose latest run failed with no bug, and once every referenced case's latest run passed and no blocking bug is open, it SHALL name `chough stage advance` to accept instead, the checkpoint's own next action shown as a sentence of its own; at accept while the native change is verifying, it SHALL say the human reviews next and SHALL never suggest an agent review: for a decision to ship it SHALL name `chough change ship <id> --close-gate "<gate>"` with the relay of REQ-cli-050, which runs the review as the human, ships and closes the gate only after the native ship (REQ-cli-059), so nothing under `.chough/` changes between `change check --commit` and finalize; for a decision not to ship, `chough checkpoint --close-gate` with `--verdict block`; with no review gate open it SHALL first name `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<review>" --holds accept --drives review` and, while SpecSync's verification counts Chough's records (REQ-records-014), SHALL say to commit that gate and run `chough change check <id>` again before the ship; and the waiting action for an open review gate SHALL name the same ship. A gate close that leaves no open gate holding the current stage (REQ-cli-050) SHALL set the checkpoint's next action to the step that decision allows, and `chough next` SHALL never name itself as the next action: `chough stage advance` after an approval or the close of a gate that drives nothing, `chough change ship <id>` after a review pass, `chough stage back --to build` after a review block, and, after a `--no-native` close, recording the next action the decision calls for with `chough checkpoint --next-action`. At accept while the native change is approved or implementing, the next valid action SHALL name the review preparation of the workflow's accept step in order, `chough change check <id> --no-commit` first when the change's deltas add or modify requirements, then the affected cases, the review gate, the commit and `chough change check <id>`, and SHALL NOT show a refused gate or a bare native status read as the action. A command that `chough next` or `chough status` shows, in the next valid action, a gate or a refusal, SHALL appear whole, whatever its length: a bound is met by cutting other text, never a command. `chough status` SHALL start with the same focused summary that `chough next` gives, at most 40 lines of text and a `summary` object first in JSON, before its full report, so the next action is never buried (BUG-0023). Decisions, completed work and open questions SHALL be read from the session's story sections (REQ-records-004), and corrections and the last actor shown as REQ-history-015 and REQ-records-007 say. Trace: LIFE-3, FLOW-13, FLOW-2, LIFE-7, LIFE-1, FLOW-12, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24.

Acceptance Criteria
- With 500 referenced stale observations, 40 awaiting-human gates and 40 blockers of 4 KiB each, 50 decisions of 4 KiB each (a checkpoint within the 1,048,576-byte cap of REQ-cli-032), 100 failed observations, 40 bugs linking the latest failure, 40 archived lesson bundles, 16 modules in the checkpoint and a native response near the parse bound, the text and JSON forms each stay within 16384 bytes, list at most 10 entries per list and state each total.
- The view lists referenced observations that are historical, removed, ambiguous (a merge left two records with that name; the row names its places) or unavailable and counts referenced current and unreferenced ones; it carries no raw native output, no observation record and no lesson text.
- The view shows the last 5 decisions newest first with the kind and reason of prefixed entries and unprefixed entries whole; the failed observation with the greatest recorded time, ties broken by the greater observation ID, with each linking bug's status; and each module's lesson source path, at most 10 with their total, with the archived bundle count and up to 3 paths, newest finalized first, matching the lesson bundles `knowledge/index.md` links.
- Two runs over the same records, and a run after file modification times change, give byte-identical text and JSON.
